A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Leak@k research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on TOFU, MUSE-News, MUSE-Books, and WMDP, together with the NPO-Fix experiment in Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark evaluations and reports additional RULE experiments, comparator results, and analyses of probabilistic leakage.

M1.justification: RULE substantially extends v1's NPO-Fix: the single forget-set augmentation and retraining stage becomes repeated generation and unlearning, with augmentation of both forget and retain sets. The procedure supports NPO, SimNPO, GradDiff, and RMU instead of only NPO (v1 Appendix F; v2 Section 4 and Appendix F). The leak@k estimator itself remains unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 removes MUSE-Books, including the Harry Potter forget questions and Fan Wiki retain coverage evaluated in v1 Table 10. TOFU forget10, MUSE-News, and WMDP-bio/MMLU coverage remain. The new RULE and diagnostic experiments use retained domains.

E2.justification: v2 adds LoUK to TOFU comparisons, NPO-SURE to MUSE-News leakage comparisons, and PMC against RULE-GradDiff in Table A6. These are verified experimental additions; most existing comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: The mitigation experiment changes from NPO-Fix's 10 initial epochs, 32 generations per forget question, and one five-epoch refinement at learning rate 10^-6 to RULE's five initial epochs and three refinement cycles at 10^-5, sampling 20 responses for 50% of forget and retain questions. New diagnostic protocols include 500 generations per MUSE-News prompt. WMDP sample coverage is ambiguous: v2 Appendix E.1 lists 200 prompts while Appendix B still specifies 1,273 questions.

E4.justification: v2 adds conditional-token probability case studies explaining leakage initiation, a TOFU analysis separating previously safe and unsafe questions to examine cancellation in average leakage, and RULE leakage–utility trajectories across training iterations (Figure 8; Appendices E.2–E.3). The earlier decoding sweeps and WMDP refusal analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed replication, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The estimator variance argument remains unchanged. The new diagnostic sample counts and averaged observations do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: TOFU ES heatmaps are revised, and v1's NPO-Fix results, including 61.9% leak@128–ES in Table A2, are replaced by RULE results under different training conditions. v2 Table A6 reports leak@128–ES of 0.004 for RULE-GradDiff versus 0.149 for PMC, with retain scores of 0.398 versus 0.235. New average-leakage and token-probability results are added, while MUSE-Books results are removed. This does not establish a controlled NPO-Fix-to-RULE performance gain.

T1.justification: The leak@k definition, unbiased estimators, variance comparison, and Appendix D proof retain the same mathematical substance. The background losses also remain unchanged. RULE adds algorithmic procedures without new theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds the evaluation metric and widespread leakage, describing NPO-Fix as insufficient. v2 makes RULE a third main contribution and claims near-zero or no TOFU leakage through 128 generations in the abstract and introduction. It also adds a claim that method rankings generally persist across decoding parameters and sample counts.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations involving an initial sensitive token increasing subsequent token confidence and opposing safe/unsafe subgroup changes concealing leakage in averages. Section 4 attributes residual memorization to fixed forget datasets and explicitly limits RULE validation to TOFU, leaving MUSE and WMDP extensions for future work.

D1.justification: v2 adds NVIDIA A40 hardware information, benchmark generation/evaluation timings, objective-specific RULE hyperparameters, and an approximately two-hour training-stage breakdown (Tables A4, A11, and A12). These extend v1's mitigation implementation disclosures. The NLI model name remains, but its explicit checkpoint URL is removed.

R1.justification: The discussion of prior probabilistic evaluation is substantially revised to acknowledge multiple sampled responses and distinguish average-case evaluation from repeated-attempt leakage. Appendix A adds extensive positioning against UNSTAR and PMC and discusses RULE's relationship to entropy regularization. Four works are newly cited, while the Transformers reference is removed.

P1.justification: v2 edits the introduction and related-work exposition, corrects the introductory SU/SFT description, moves dataset descriptions from Section 3 to Appendix B, and reorganizes Appendix E into setup, diagnostic, and benchmark subsections. RULE receives a dedicated section, while much of the metric exposition and existing benchmark narrative is retained.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the introductory MUSE-News curve display with a TOFU/RULE plot, adds the token-probability illustration and RULE trajectory figure, and expands comparator rows in heatmaps. Several example tables move from the main text into appendices, and new diagnostic, comparison, hyperparameter, and runtime tables substantially revise the visual organization.

improvement.justification: The new token-probability and safe/unsafe subgroup analyses strengthen the empirical rationale for leak@k. RULE's iteration/utility study, PMC comparison, and implementation details also develop the constructive contribution beyond v1's limited NPO-Fix test. These gains are tempered by removing MUSE-Books evidence, including GradDiff's zero leakage, and by the abstract's unqualified 'no information leakage' wording despite the nonzero 0.004 result in Table A6.
